line: Jung on spiritus and pneuma: air in motion, spirit and soul, Mercurius, and body, soul and spirit.

sections.title: Air in motion
sections.line: Pneuma and spiritus as air, wind and breath: CW13 pdf p244; CW18 ¶359.

quotes.quote: The texts often use the terms pneuma and spiritus in the original concrete sense of “air in motion.”
Spirit, spiritus, or pneuma really means air, wind, breath; spiritus and pneuma in their archetypal character are dynamic and half-substantial agencies

sections.title: Spirit and soul
sections.line: Spirit and soul in the alchemical texts: CW13 pdf p245, p243 and p248.

quotes.quote: “Soul” represents a higher concept than “spirit” in the sense of air or gas.
something non-material and finer than mere air
As has already been indicated, the psychic nature of the arcane substance did not escape the alchemists; indeed, they actually defined it as “spirit” and “soul.”
whatever else spirit and soul may be, from the phenomenological point of view they are psychic structures.

sections.title: Mercurius and the spiritus
sections.line: The spiritus mercurii and the spiritus mercurialis: CW13 ¶171; CW12 ¶172, ¶84 and ¶518.

quotes.quote: The balsam is the life principle, the spiritus mercurii, and it more or less coincides with the Paracelsan concept of the Iliaster.
Chemically this term denotes quicksilver, but philosophically it means the spiritus vitae, or even the world-soul
The spiritus mercurialis (fig. 23) is the alchemists’ guide (Hermes Psychopompos: cf. fig. 146), and their tempter; he is their good luck and their ruin.
another symbol of Mercurius, who, in his volatile form of spiritus, is a parallel of the Holy Ghost.

sections.title: Body, soul and spirit
sections.line: Body, soul and spirit, and von Franz on pneuma, soul and body as the One: CW12 ¶243; von Franz, Number and Time, pdf p282.

quotes.quote: and to consist of body, soul, and spirit
Pneuma, soul, and body then become “the One in which the mystery is concealed.”
This One is a statue which was born of fire; it unites spirit, soul, and body and contains the four elements within itself.
quotes.voice: von Franz, quoting an alchemical text

sections.title: Spirit and the life of the mind
sections.line: Spirit in the mind: CW13 pdf p247; CW8 ¶621.

quotes.quote: In many of the passages it remains doubtful whether spiritus means spirit in an abstract sense.
One thing alone seems clear: just as the "living being" is the quintessence of life in the body, so "spirit" is the quintessence of the life of the mind
